main_text.p: gefimæ nonæ , à morte Alexandri Ma-gni sexagesimus primus.Eo anno fluen-te Antigonus rex, alterâ victoriâ in-gente ex Gallis regnum suum turban-tibus elatus, recordatus eorum , quæ Athenienses in patrem suum deliquerant , comparatis ingentibus armato-rum copiis, urbem eorum terrâ mari-que obsedit , nec antè finem ejus fecit, quàm Athenas sese dedere compulisset, frustrà auxiliis à Ptolemæo Ægypti rege & civitate Spartanâ contra obsiden-tem ad sublevandos obsessos submissis. Tum rursus, libertate reliqua incolumi, præsidium Macedonicum urbi impositum. Quod licet decennio post eodem permittente rege inde amotum fuit, tamen urbs in clientela Macedonum mansit , & eorum partibus adhæsit, quandiu Antigonus vixit, (vixit autem post id tempus annos quasi xvii, ) & post eum Demetrius ejus filius , qui re-gnavit annos x. Retinebant enim in potestate suâ Macedones Piræum , Mu-nychiam, Salaminem , Sunium, & At-ticæ quædam loca alia , quibus velut cincta civitas commovere se non po-terat : imò partium Macedonicarum studium singulare præ se ferre necef-sum habebat. Verū extincto Demetrio, [illegible, ~1 letter]um Macedoniæ jam præsideret Anti-gonus

page.notes: The first word of the page is a fragment and is kept as such. The word at the start of the last line is partly hidden by the binding, so only "um" can be read; the letter before it is illegible. Long s is printed as s in the scan and is given as plain s. The final "gonus" completes "Anti-gonus" from the line above. Show-through and binding shadows at the left and bottom edges are left out.
